name: NK Maribor
content:
NK Maribor is a professional football club based in Maribor, Slovenia, founded in 1960. Known by the nickname “The Purples,” the club has become one of the strongest symbols of Slovenian football, especially in the Styria region. Since the creation of the Slovenian top division after independence, Maribor has remained one of the country’s most important and consistent football institutions.

The club is the most successful team in Slovenian football history, having won a record number of league titles and domestic trophies. Maribor experienced periods of dominance, particularly in the late 1990s and early 2000s, and later returned to the top with another successful era in the 2010s. Before Slovenia became independent, the club also competed in the Yugoslav football system and reached the top division during that period.

Maribor has also achieved important success in European competitions and became the first Slovenian club to reach the group stages of both the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Europa League. The club plays its home matches at Ljudski vrt Stadium and has a passionate fan base. One of the biggest traditions surrounding the team is its fierce rivalry with Olimpija Ljubljana in the famous Eternal Derby.

name: ND Gorica
content:
ND Gorica is a Slovenian football club based in Nova Gorica that was founded in 1947. Nicknamed “The Roses,” the club has become one of the most recognized football institutions in western Slovenia. Throughout its history, Gorica has represented the football tradition of the Goriška region and has played an important role in the development of Slovenian football.

Before Slovenia’s independence, the club competed within the Yugoslav football system and gradually built its reputation. Following independence in 1991, Gorica became one of the founding members of the Slovenian top division and soon emerged as a major force in domestic football. The club won its first Slovenian league title in the 1995–96 season and later enjoyed its most successful era in the mid-2000s.

Gorica is among the most successful clubs in Slovenia, having won multiple league championships and domestic cup titles. The team has also participated in European competitions and built a strong football identity through memorable seasons and rivalries. The club plays its home matches at Nova Gorica Sports Park and remains an important name in Slovenian football history.

name: NK Olimpija
content:
NK Olimpija Ljubljana was a Slovenian football club based in Ljubljana that existed from 1945 until 2005. Founded originally as NK Enotnost, the club adopted the name Olimpija in 1962 and became one of the most recognizable football institutions in Slovenia. Nicknamed “The Dragons” and “The Green and Whites,” the club developed a strong identity connected to the city of Ljubljana and its symbols.

During the Yugoslav era, Olimpija competed within the national league system and spent many seasons in the Yugoslav First League, particularly between the late 1960s and late 1980s. After Slovenia gained independence in 1991, the club quickly became one of the dominant forces in the new domestic championship. Olimpija won four Slovenian league titles and four national cup trophies while also participating in several European competitions.

The club played its home matches at Bežigrad Stadium and built a passionate fan culture led by the Green Dragons supporters group. Despite its football success and historical importance, financial difficulties eventually caused severe problems. In 2005, the club was dissolved because of large debts, although a successor club was founded shortly afterward and later continued the Olimpija football tradition in Ljubljana.

name: NK Olimpija Ljubljana
content:
NK Olimpija Ljubljana is a Slovenian professional football club based in the capital city, Ljubljana. The modern club was founded in 2005 following the dissolution of the original NK Olimpija due to financial problems. It began competing in the lower tiers of Slovenian football and quickly progressed through the league system, establishing itself as a continuation of the city’s long football tradition. The club is widely known by its nicknames “The Dragons” and “The Green and Whites,” reflecting the city’s symbol and traditional team colors.

After its rapid rise through the divisions, Olimpija returned to the Slovenian top flight and became one of the leading clubs in the country. The team plays in the Slovenian PrvaLiga and has developed into a consistent title contender. Since its return to the top level, Olimpija has won multiple league championships and domestic cup trophies, often competing closely with rivals such as NK Maribor. The club’s success has helped re-establish Ljubljana as a central hub of Slovenian football.

Olimpija plays its home matches at the modern Stožice Stadium, one of the largest football venues in Slovenia. The club is also known for its strong supporter base, the Green Dragons, who are among the most active ultras groups in the country. With a strong identity, domestic success, and regular participation in European competitions, NK Olimpija Ljubljana remains one of the most influential and recognizable football clubs in Slovenian football today.

name: NK Celje
content:
NK Celje is a Slovenian professional football club based in the city of Celje, founded in 1919 as SK Celje. Throughout its long history, the club has undergone several name changes and reorganizations, including periods as NK Kladivar and NK Publikum, before eventually returning to the name NK Celje. It is one of the oldest active football clubs in Slovenia and has played an important role in the development of football in the region. The team is commonly known by its nickname “The Counts,” reflecting its identity and tradition.

During the Yugoslav era, Celje competed in the national league system, spending most of its time in the lower divisions but occasionally reaching higher levels of competition. After Slovenia gained independence in 1991, the club became a founding member of the Slovenian PrvaLiga and has remained a consistent participant ever since. Over time, Celje established itself as a stable top-flight club, regularly competing in domestic league and cup competitions and gradually improving its competitiveness within Slovenian football.

The club achieved its first major successes in the mid-2000s, including winning the Slovenian Cup, and later went on to secure its first league title in the 2019–20 season. Celje has since added further league and cup victories, strengthening its status as one of the leading clubs in the country. It plays its home matches at Stadion Z’dežele, a modern stadium in Celje, and has also taken part in European competitions, representing Slovenia on the international stage.

name: NK Domžale
content:
NK Domžale is a Slovenian professional football club based in the town of Domžale, founded in 1920 as SK Disk. For most of its early history, the club competed in regional and lower-tier competitions within the Yugoslav football system. Although it did not establish itself as a major force during the Yugoslav era, it gradually developed a stable football structure and identity that later became important in Slovenian football.

After Slovenia’s independence in 1991, Domžale became part of the newly formed national league system and initially faced mixed results, including relegation from the top division. The club’s modern rise began in the early 2000s, when improved management and coaching stability helped it return to the Slovenian PrvaLiga. This period marked a turning point, as Domžale quickly transformed from a lower-table side into a serious competitor in domestic football.

The club’s most successful era came in the mid-2000s, when it won back-to-back Slovenian league titles in the 2006–07 and 2007–08 seasons. Domžale also achieved success in domestic cup competitions and took part in European tournaments, gaining international experience against stronger opposition. The team plays its home matches at Domžale Sports Park and is known for developing players and maintaining a strong focus on youth development within Slovenian football.

name: FC Koper
content:
FC Koper is a Slovenian professional football club based in the coastal city of Koper, founded in 1920 under its original name Circolo Sportivo Capodistriano. Over the decades, the club went through several reorganizations, name changes, and mergers, reflecting the complex political and sporting history of the region. After World War II and the incorporation of the area into Yugoslavia, the club developed within the Yugoslav football system and became one of the more notable teams from the Slovenian Littoral region.

Following Slovenia’s independence in 1991, Koper joined the newly formed Slovenian league system and competed in the PrvaLiga. The club experienced a mix of mid-table finishes, relegations, and financial instability during the 1990s and early 2000s, including periods of restructuring and sponsorship-based name changes. Despite these difficulties, Koper gradually re-established itself as a competitive top-flight side and also gained experience in European competitions, marking important milestones in its modern development.

The club’s greatest achievement came in the 2009–10 season, when FC Koper won the Slovenian PrvaLiga title for the first time. They have also claimed domestic cup success and continued to be a strong presence in Slovenian football, although financial and administrative challenges have occasionally disrupted stability, including a temporary relegation due to licensing issues in 2017. Koper plays its home matches at Stadion Bonifika and remains an important club known for resilience, periodic success, and its role in coastal Slovenian football.

name: NŠ Mura
content:
NŠ Mura is a Slovenian professional football club based in Murska Sobota. The current club was founded in 2012 after the dissolution of ND Mura 05 due to financial problems. It was established as a new project built around a youth academy structure and quickly restarted its journey in the lower tiers of Slovenian football. The club is commonly known as “The Black and Whites” and has developed a strong local identity in the Prekmurje region.

Starting from the fourth division in the 2013–14 season, Mura achieved rapid progress through the Slovenian league system. After consecutive promotions, the club reached the Slovenian PrvaLiga in 2018, marking its return to top-flight football in a very short time. This rise was followed by immediate competitiveness in the top division, as the team established itself as a solid mid-table side and soon began challenging for higher positions.

The club’s biggest successes came in the 2020–21 period, when Mura won its first major trophy by claiming the Slovenian Cup and followed it with its first national league title the same season. These achievements also led to European competition appearances, including participation in UEFA tournaments and a historic group-stage campaign. Mura plays its home matches at Fazanerija Stadium in Murska Sobota and is recognized for its passionate supporters and strong community identity.

name: ND Mura 05
content:
ND Mura 05 was a Slovenian football club based in Murska Sobota, founded in 2005 following the dissolution of NK Mura due to financial problems. The club was created as a continuation of local football tradition and took over the youth structure of its predecessor. It began competing in the lower divisions of Slovenian football, with the aim of rebuilding competitive senior-level football in the region. The team played its home matches at Fazanerija Stadium, the traditional football ground in the city.

After its formation, ND Mura 05 progressed steadily through the Slovenian league system. Starting from the lower tiers, the club achieved multiple promotions and eventually reached the Slovenian PrvaLiga. Its rise was particularly rapid, and within a few years it had established itself as a top-flight side. The club’s best period came in the early 2010s, when it competed in the highest division and gained national attention for its performances and development.

Despite its sporting progress, ND Mura 05 faced serious financial difficulties that ultimately led to its downfall. In the 2012–13 season, the club was unable to secure a license to continue competing at the professional level, resulting in its dissolution in 2013. Following its collapse, a new club, NŠ Mura, was founded to continue football in Murska Sobota, but ND Mura 05 is remembered as an important transitional project in the region’s football history.

name: NK Mura
content:
NK Mura was a Slovenian football club based in Murska Sobota, founded on 16 August 1924. It was one of the oldest clubs in the Prekmurje region and became an important part of local sporting identity. The club played its home matches at the Fazanerija Stadium and was widely supported in its region, developing a strong fan base known for its loyalty and passion. Over time, Mura became a recognizable name in Slovenian football.

The club experienced its strongest period after Slovenia’s independence in 1991. During the 1990s, NK Mura achieved notable domestic success, including finishing as runners-up in the Slovenian top division on multiple occasions and winning the Slovenian Football Cup in 1995. This success also led to participation in European competitions, although the club was generally unable to progress beyond the early qualifying rounds. Despite financial limitations, Mura remained competitive and produced several strong seasons in the national league.

In the early 2000s, the club faced serious financial difficulties, which eventually led to instability and the inability to secure a competition license. After finishing the 2004–05 season, NK Mura was dissolved in 2005. Following its disappearance, successor clubs were later formed in Murska Sobota to continue the football tradition, but the original NK Mura is remembered for its historical role, passionate supporters, and its contribution to Slovenian football development.

name: NK Primorje
content:
NK Primorje was a Slovenian football club based in Ajdovščina, founded in 1924. The club became an important representative of football in the Vipava Valley region and spent much of its early history competing in lower divisions of the Yugoslav football system. After Slovenia gained independence in 1991, Primorje gradually established itself as one of the more stable provincial clubs in the national league structure, playing its home matches at the Ajdovščina City Stadium.

In the Slovenian top division, NK Primorje became a consistent participant, especially during the 1990s and 2000s. The club achieved notable success during this period, including finishing as runners-up in the Slovenian PrvaLiga in the 1996–97 and 2001–02 seasons. It also reached multiple Slovenian Cup finals, although it did not manage to win the competition. Primorje additionally competed in European tournaments, gaining experience against international opposition while representing Slovenian football abroad.

Despite its sporting achievements, the club struggled with financial difficulties, which eventually became unsustainable. Due to heavy debts and failure to obtain a competition license, NK Primorje was dissolved after the 2010–11 season. A successor club was later founded in Ajdovščina to continue the football tradition in the region, but the original NK Primorje is remembered for its strong league performances and its role in establishing football identity in western Slovenia.

name: NK Rudar Velenje
content:
NK Rudar Velenje is a Slovenian football club based in the industrial city of Velenje, founded in 1948. The club’s name “Rudar” means “miner,” reflecting the region’s strong mining heritage, and its nickname “Knapi” (The Miners) is closely tied to this identity. It plays its home matches at the Ob Jezeru City Stadium, which has been its home ground since the mid-20th century. The club has long been an important part of the local sporting culture in the Šalek Valley.

Throughout its history, Rudar Velenje developed through the Yugoslav football system, where it achieved notable success at the republic level, including winning regional competitions and earning promotion to higher tiers. After Slovenia became independent in 1991, the club became a regular participant in the Slovenian top division. During the 1990s and 2000s, it experienced some of its strongest periods, including high league finishes and domestic cup success, establishing itself as a competitive first-division team.

One of the club’s greatest achievements came in the 1997–98 season, when Rudar Velenje won the Slovenian Cup, which also allowed it to participate in European competitions. The club has also finished near the top of the national league on several occasions and competed in UEFA tournaments such as the Cup Winners’ Cup and Europa League. In recent years, Rudar has spent time between the top division and the second tier, but it remains an important and historically successful club in Slovenian football.

name: NK Izola
content:
NK Izola was a Slovenian football club based in the coastal town of Izola, founded in 1923. The club developed under various names during its early history as the region changed political and sporting systems, including periods under Italian and Yugoslav football structures. It became an important representative of football in the Slovenian Littoral region and played its home matches at the Izola City Stadium, building a strong local identity and fan support over many decades.

The club experienced its peak period in the early 1990s after Slovenia gained independence, when it competed in the Slovenian PrvaLiga. During this time, NK Izola spent several seasons in the top division and also took part in European competition, including a UEFA Cup appearance against Benfica in the 1992–93 season. Despite these highlights, the club generally struggled to establish itself among the strongest Slovenian teams, often fighting to maintain top-flight status.

Financial difficulties eventually became the club’s main problem, and after the 1995–96 season NK Izola was dissolved due to heavy debt and organizational instability. Following its collapse, a successor club was formed in 1996, but it is considered a separate legal entity and does not carry the original club’s records. The original NK Izola remains remembered for its early football tradition, brief top-division presence, and its role in coastal Slovenian football history.

name: NK IB 1975 Ljubljana
content:
NK IB 1975 Ljubljana is a Slovenian football club based in Ljubljana that was originally founded in 1975 as NK Ježica. The club spent its early decades competing mainly in lower regional leagues within the Yugoslav football system and later the Slovenian league structure. Over time it went through several reorganizations and name changes, eventually becoming known as NK Factor Ježica and later NK Interblock after a takeover and rebranding in the mid-2000s. This period marked the beginning of its rise through the national football pyramid.

The club experienced its most successful era in the 2000s after strong financial backing and restructuring. It reached the Slovenian top division and achieved notable success, including winning major domestic trophies. Under the Interblock name, the club won the Slovenian Cup twice in consecutive seasons and also secured the Slovenian Supercup. During this time, it also competed in European competitions, representing Slovenia in UEFA tournaments.

After 2010, the club went through further changes, including cooperation and partial mergers with other Ljubljana-based football projects. The senior team eventually withdrew from professional competition in 2012 due to organizational instability but was later re-established and continued playing in lower divisions. Today, NK IB 1975 Ljubljana operates mainly within the lower tiers of Slovenian football, focusing on rebuilding its structure and youth development.

name: NK Rogaška
content:
NK Rogaška is a Slovenian football club based in Rogaška Slatina that was founded in 1999 following the dissolution of the former club NK Steklar. The new club was established to continue the football tradition in the town and began competing in the lower tiers of Slovenian football. Over time, Rogaška gradually built its structure and identity, representing a small spa town with a strong sporting culture and limited resources compared to larger Slovenian clubs.

During its development, the club spent many years moving through the lower regional and amateur divisions before achieving steady progress through the league system. After multiple promotions across the 2010s and early 2020s, Rogaška reached higher competitive levels and eventually climbed into the professional tiers of Slovenian football. This rise marked a significant turnaround for the club, as it transformed from a lower-league side into a competitive team capable of challenging stronger opponents.

The club’s most notable achievements came in the early 2020s, when it won titles in the lower divisions and reached the Slovenian PrvaLiga for the first time in its history. Rogaška also achieved a historic milestone by winning the Slovenian Cup in the 2023–24 season, one of the biggest successes in its short modern history. Despite later facing licensing issues and relegation, the club remains an important example of rapid progress in Slovenian football and continues to represent its local community.

name: NK Korotan Prevalje
content:
NK Korotan Prevalje was a Slovenian football club based in Prevalje, founded in 1933. It became one of the traditional clubs in the Koroška region and developed its identity over many decades of competing in Yugoslav and later Slovenian football systems. The club played its home matches at Stadion na Prevaljah and was known for its local support and strong regional presence.

After Slovenia gained independence, Korotan experienced its most successful period. The club competed in the Slovenian PrvaLiga for several seasons, becoming a stable top-division side during the 1990s and early 2000s. Its peak came around the 1999–2000 season, when it achieved a high league finish, reached the Slovenian Cup final, and also participated in European competition, marking the most successful chapter in its history.

Despite sporting achievements, the club struggled with serious financial difficulties in the early 2000s. During the 2002–03 season, Korotan was unable to complete its league campaign and was eventually dissolved due to debt and organizational problems. A successor club was later founded in Prevalje, but the original NK Korotan remains remembered for its rise to the top division and its important role in Slovenian football history.

name: NK Dravograd
content:
NK Dravograd is a Slovenian football club based in the town of Dravograd, founded in 1948. The club originally started under the name NK Turbina and later went through several reorganizations as football developed in the region. It has long been an important sports institution in the Koroška region, representing a small but football-active community near the Austrian border. The team plays its home matches at the Dravograd Sports Centre, which has a modest capacity and serves as the club’s traditional ground.

After Slovenia’s independence in 1991, NK Dravograd rose through the national football system and reached its most successful period in the late 1990s and early 2000s. The club competed in the Slovenian top division on multiple occasions, first reaching the PrvaLiga in the 1994–95 season. It also spent several seasons moving between the first and second tiers, achieving promotion successes in the second division and establishing itself as a competitive mid-level Slovenian club.

One of the club’s notable achievements was reaching the final of the Slovenian Cup in the early 2000s, which marked the peak of its competitive success. However, after this period, Dravograd gradually declined and eventually settled into lower divisions of Slovenian football. Today, the club is known more for its historical role and contribution to regional football development, as well as for producing players who later moved on to higher levels of competition.

name: NK Nafta 1903
content:
NK Nafta 1903 is a Slovenian football club based in Lendava, founded in 2012 as a phoenix club after the dissolution of NK Nafta Lendava due to financial problems. The club was created to continue the football tradition in the region and is widely regarded as the modern successor representing Lendava’s historic football identity. It plays its home matches at the Lendava Sports Park and has become an important sporting symbol for the local community.

Starting from the lower tiers of Slovenian football, Nafta 1903 quickly progressed through the league system. After its foundation, the club climbed from regional competitions into the Slovenian Third League and later reached the Second League. Through consistent performances and stable development, it established itself as one of the stronger teams outside the top division, regularly competing for promotion spots.

In the 2023–24 season, Nafta 1903 finished near the top of the Slovenian Second League and secured promotion to the PrvaLiga, marking its debut in the top flight. The club also achieved success in domestic cup competitions at regional level during its rise. Today, NK Nafta 1903 continues to develop as a competitive professional club, representing one of the key football stories of rapid progression in Slovenian football.

name: NK Bravo
content:
NK Bravo is a Slovenian professional football club based in Ljubljana, founded in 2006. The club was created as a youth-focused football project and gradually developed into a competitive senior team. In its early years, Bravo competed in the lower regional and amateur divisions of Slovenian football, slowly building a structured academy system and a reputation for developing young players. The club is commonly associated with the Šiška district of Ljubljana and plays its home matches at the Šiška Sports Park.

During the 2010s, NK Bravo experienced a rapid rise through the Slovenian football league system. After progressing through regional leagues, it reached the Slovenian Second League and eventually won promotion to the top division for the first time in the 2019–20 season. Since then, Bravo has established itself as a stable PrvaLiga side, often finishing in mid-table positions while maintaining a strong emphasis on youth development and long-term sporting structure.

In recent seasons, NK Bravo has also taken part in domestic cup competitions, including reaching the final of the Slovenian Cup, and has made appearances in European qualifiers. While not considered one of Slovenia’s traditional powerhouse clubs, Bravo is widely recognized for its modern development model, focus on player progression, and steady growth within Slovenian football.

name: NK Aluminij
content:
NK Aluminij is a Slovenian football club based in Kidričevo, founded in 1946. The club is traditionally known by the nicknames “Šumari” (The Foresters) and “Rdeče-beli” (The Red and Whites). It plays its home matches at the Športni park Aluminij, a small stadium that has been modernized and expanded over time. The club has long been an important representative of football in the Štajerska region and has a strong local identity.

Historically, Aluminij competed in the Yugoslav football system, where it achieved one of its early successes by winning the Slovenian Republic League in the 1965–66 season. After Slovenia became independent in 1991, the club started in the lower divisions and gradually progressed through the system. By the late 1990s, it had reached the Slovenian Second League and became a stable competitor at that level, often challenging for promotion to the top flight.

In the 21st century, NK Aluminij established itself as a regular presence in Slovenian professional football, moving between the first and second divisions. The club achieved multiple promotions to the PrvaLiga and has also reached the final of the Slovenian Cup. Despite its relatively small size and limited resources, Aluminij is known for its strong organization, youth development, and resilience in Slovenian football.

name: NK Brinje Grosuplje
content:
NK Brinje Grosuplje is a Slovenian football club based in the town of Grosuplje. It was founded in 2003 as a newly established club after the dissolution of the former NK Grosuplje, with the aim of continuing football tradition in the area. The club is legally considered a separate entity and does not inherit the history or honours of its predecessor, but it has become the main football representative of the town. It plays its home matches at Brinje Stadium in Grosuplje.

After its foundation, Brinje Grosuplje started competing in the lower tiers of Slovenian football and gradually built its sporting structure. The club spent many years in regional and lower national divisions before beginning its rise through the league system. Through steady development, improved organization, and strong youth work, it eventually progressed into higher competitive levels of Slovenian football and established itself as a serious club in the national pyramid.

In recent years, NK Brinje Grosuplje has competed in the Slovenian Second League and has become one of the more stable and competitive teams at that level. The club has consistently finished in the upper part of the table, challenging for promotion to the top division. Alongside its sporting progress, Brinje has also invested in infrastructure and youth development, strengthening its long-term ambitions in Slovenian football.
